SPP respectfully requests that the Commission establish a shortened seven (7) day
comment period, and issue an order accepting the proposed Tariff revisions as
expeditiously as possible to facilitate implementation before the commencement of the
upcoming Winter Season, which commences on December 1, 2026.

I.     BACKGROUND

In the September Filing, SPP submitted revisions to the SPP Open Access Transmission
Tariff 4 to implement an interim supply adequacy structure for the SPP West Balancing
Authority Area (“SPP West BAA”).

Several parties filed motions to intervene.5 On September 25, 2026, Basin,6 Guzman,7 and
WAPA8 filed comments. On September 25, 2026, the SPP MMU filed a protest and
comments.9 On October 13, 2026, SPP filed an answer in response to the comments and
protest.10

In the Deficiency Letter, the Commission directed SPP to provide additional information
required to process the filing. The Commission required responses be submitted within
thirty (30) days of the date of the request for additional information. In this instant filing,
SPP submits its responses to the specific questions raised in the Deficiency Letter.

II.      RESPONSE TO DEFICIENCY LETTER

Question 1:

SPP proposes to assess a market inadequacy obligation charge when an Asset
Owner’s Obligations in the SPP West BAA are greater than the Asset Owner’s
Available Energy and to distribute the revenues received according to formulae in
proposed sections 8.6.47(1)(a) and 8.6.48(1)(a) of Attachment AE of its Tariff. Under
the proposed formulae, the distribution amount equals the Market Inadequacy
Obligation Amount multiplied by the “West BAA Asset Owner Adequate Ratio
Share,” which is defined as “the ratio share of each Energy-adequate Asset Owner’s
share of adequate MWs divided by all Energy-adequate Asset Owner’s adequate MW
in the SPP West Balancing Authority Area.”11 However, the term “adequate MW”
is not defined in the SPP Tariff. For example, it is not clear whether the term refers
to all Available Energy MWs of an Energy-adequate Asset Owner, only those MWs
above its Obligations, or a different value.

Please clarify the meaning of “adequate MWs” in proposed sections 8.6.47(1)(a)(ii)
and 8.6.48(1)(a)(ii) of Attachment AE, including any relevant equations. Please
explain why the resulting revenue distribution is just and reasonable and not unduly
discriminatory or preferential.

Response to Question No. 1:

      A. Clarification of “Adequate MWs”

The phrase “adequate MWs” refers to the amount by which an Asset Owner’s Available
Energy exceeds its Obligations during the applicable Operating Hour. Accordingly, the
term “adequate MWs” does not represent the entirety of an Asset Owner's Available
Energy, but rather the portion of its Available Energy that exceeds the amount necessary
to satisfy its own Obligations. The proposed distribution methodology, explained in more
detail below, recognizes the Energy an Asset Owner maintains in excess of its own
commitments, rather than rewarding an Asset Owner merely for possessing a large
portfolio of Resources. An Asset Owner whose Available Energy equals or falls below its
Obligation has an adequate MW quantity of zero and receives no distribution.

The specific equations reflecting the meaning of “adequate MWs” are set forth in proposed




11
         Proposed Tariff, Att. AE, § 8.6.47, § 8.6.47(1)(a)(ii) (emphasis added); id. § 8.6.48,
         § 8.6.48(1)(a)(ii) (emphasis added).
 The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese
November 5, 2026
Page 4


revisions to SPP’s Settlements Calculation Guide,12 which are attached hereto as
Attachment A. The equations reflect that the adequacy quantity for each Asset Owner is
calculated by determining the difference between the Asset Owner's Available Energy and
its Obligations, with only the amount of Available Energy exceeding Obligations included
in the calculation.

For the Day-Ahead Reliability Unit Commitment ("Day-Ahead RUC") evaluation, the
calculation uses the Asset Owner’s Available Energy and Obligations associated with the
Day-Ahead RUC process.13 For the Pre-Operating Hour evaluation, the calculation uses
the corresponding Available Energy and Obligations determined through the Intra-Day
RUC process.14

Once the surplus quantity is determined for each Energy-adequate Asset Owner, SPP
calculates the SPP West BAA Asset Owner Adequate Ratio Share by dividing the
individual Asset Owner's surplus MWs by the total surplus MWs of all Energy-adequate
Asset Owners within the SPP West BAA for the applicable Operating Hour.15

The resulting ratio is then multiplied by the total market inadequacy obligation revenues
collected from Energy-inadequate Asset Owners for the applicable Operating Hour to
determine the amount distributed to each Energy-adequate Asset Owner.16 The same
proportional distribution methodology applies to both the Day-Ahead RUC and Pre-

Operating Hour market inadequacy obligation revenue distributions.17 For example,
assume that three Asset Owners have surplus quantities of 100 MW, 200 MW, and 300
MW, respectively, resulting in a total of 600 surplus MWs within the SPP West BAA.
Under the proposed methodology, the Asset Owners would receive approximately 16.67%,
33.33%, and 50% of the applicable market inadequacy obligation revenues, respectively.
The distribution is therefore directly proportional to the amount by which each Asset
Owner’s Available Energy exceeds its Obligations.

     B. Justification for the Revenue Distribution Methodology

The proposed distribution methodology is just and reasonable because it allocates revenues
collected from Asset Owners that fail to satisfy their Obligations to those Asset Owners
that maintain surplus Energy available to support the SPP West BAA during Emergency
Conditions. By basing each Asset Owner's distribution on the amount of Energy available
in excess of its own Obligations, rather than its total Available Energy, the proposed
methodology establishes a direct relationship between the revenues received and the Asset
Owner's incremental contribution to energy adequacy within the SPP West BAA.

An Asset Owner that maintains only sufficient Energy to satisfy its own Obligations has
fulfilled its individual responsibility but has not made additional Energy available to
address potential shortfalls attributable to other Asset Owners. Conversely, an Asset Owner
that maintains Energy in excess of its Obligations contributes to the overall adequacy of
the SPP West BAA beyond what is necessary to satisfy its own requirements. Allocating
revenues in proportion to that surplus appropriately recognizes the additional contribution
made by such Asset Owners. Moreover, distributing revenues based on total Available
Energy would compensate Asset Owners based on the size of their Resource portfolios or
the relative magnitude of their Obligations, rather than the extent to which they maintain
surplus Energy available to support the SPP West BAA during Emergency Conditions.
Accordingly, the proposed methodology reasonably distinguishes between Energy
maintained to satisfy an Asset Owner's own Obligations and surplus Energy that
contributes to the broader reliability needs of the SPP West BAA, ensuring that revenues
are allocated in a manner consistent with the reliability objectives of the proposed
construct.

The structure is not unduly discriminatory or preferential because it applies uniformly to
all Asset Owners in the SPP West BAA. Each Asset Owner is subject to the same
Obligation calculation, the same Available Energy determination, and the same formula
for charges and distributions. The differences in outcome among Asset Owners result
solely from differences in their own energy positions relative to their Obligations, which
is a non-comparable circumstance that justifies different treatment. In this manner, the
proposed structure aligns financial implications with each Asset Owner's contribution to

energy adequacy and supports reliability within the SPP West BAA during the interim
period preceding application of SPP’s resource adequacy framework to the SPP West
BAA.

Question 2:

SPP’s proposed revisions to sections 8.6.45 and 8.6.46 in Attachment AE of its Tariff
describe the market inadequacy obligation charge that SPP will assess to an Asset
Owner when (1) the Asset Owner’s Obligation is greater than its Available Energy,
and (2) “the SPP West Balancing Authority Area … is operating under Emergency
Conditions.”18 The Tariff currently defines an Emergency Condition as “[a]
condition or situation determined by [SPP] that is imminently likely to cause a
material adverse effect on the security of, or damage to the Transmission System.”19

Please explain whether and how SPP will notify Asset Owners that it is entering into
Emergency Conditions, which serves as the basis for assessing the market inadequacy
obligation charge under sections 8.6.45 and 8.6.46.

Response to Question No. 2:

SPP will notify Market Participants, including those representing Asset Owners20 within
the SPP West BAA, when it declares operating conditions that constitute “Emergency
Conditions.” SPP will follow the same procedures it follows today for notifying Market
Participants of grid conditions.




18

       Market Inadequacy Obligation Amount), 8.6.46 (Pre-Operating Hour Market
       Inadequacy Obligation Amount).
19
       Tariff, Part I, § 1 (Definitions E).
20
       SPP communicates directly with Market Participants, rather than individual Asset
       Owners, because Market Participants are the entities registered with SPP and
       responsible for representing Asset Owners in the Integrated Marketplace. SPP does
       not maintain a direct contractual relationship with Asset Owners in their capacity
       as Asset Owners. Accordingly, notifications concerning Emergency Conditions
       will be provided to the applicable Market Participants, which are responsible for
       communicating such information to the Asset Owners they represent.
 The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese
November 5, 2026
Page 7


Specifically, Section 4.7 of the SPP BA Emergency Operating Plan21 identifies various
methods through which SPP can communicate operating conditions with stakeholders,
including the Inter-Control Center Communications Protocol (“ICCP”), electronic
notifications, and other voice and data communications.22 Generally, SPP provides
notifications concerning changing grid conditions through its Grid Notice distribution list
and through its publicly available Current Grid Conditions webpage.23

In summary, SPP's existing operational notification procedures provide Market
Participants with notice of the conditions underlying the potential assessment of the
proposed market inadequacy obligation charges.

III.   REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED CONSIDERATION AND SHORTENED
       COMMENT PERIOD

SPP respectfully requests that the Commission afford expedited consideration to this
deficiency response and establish a shortened comment period of seven (7) days. Pursuant
to 18 C.F.R. § 35.8, the Commission has discretion to establish a comment period shorter
than the ordinary twenty-one (21) days.

Expedited consideration is warranted to facilitate timely Commission action on SPP’s
proposed revisions prior to the commencement of the upcoming Winter Season, which
begins on December 1, 2026. As explained in SPP’s September Filing, the proposed
revisions are intended to address reliability concerns associated with energy adequacy in
the SPP West BAA by establishing financial incentives for Asset Owners to maintain
sufficient energy to satisfy their Obligations during Emergency Conditions. Timely
implementation is particularly important as SPP approaches the Winter Season, when
extreme weather conditions, increased electricity demand, and potential generation outages
may place additional strain on available energy supplies. Otherwise, the SPP West BAA
risks entering the Winter Season without the proposed interim mechanism designed to
encourage adequate energy availability during periods of heightened reliability risk.

SPP further submits that a shortened comment period is appropriate because (1) the instant
filing responds to the specific questions raised in the Commission's deficiency letter
concerning a proposal that has already been subject to notice and an opportunity for

       Southwest Power Pool, Inc., SPP BA Emergency Operating Plan, available at:
       https://www.spp.org/spp-documents-filings/?id=34055.
22
       SPP BA Emergency Operating Plan at Section 4.7.
23
       See, e.g., Southwest Power Pool, Inc., “Current                Grid Conditions,”
       https://spp.org/markets-operations/current-grid-conditions/     (last  accessed
       November 3, 2026).
 The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese
November 5, 2026
Page 8


comment; (2) SPP has not proposed any additional Tariff revisions in this deficiency
response; (3) interested parties have therefore had an opportunity to evaluate the underlying
proposal; and (4) the reliability concerns underlying SPP's proposal weigh in favor of
prompt consideration, particularly given the limited time remaining before the
commencement of the Winter Season.

For these reasons, SPP respectfully requests that the Commission establish a seven (7) day
comment period and issue an order accepting the proposed Tariff revisions as expeditiously
as practicable to facilitate implementation before the commencement of the upcoming
Winter Season.

IV.    REQUEST FOR REVISED EFFECTIVE DATE

In its September Filing, SPP requested an effective date of November 11, 2026, for the
proposed Tariff revisions. However, given the limited number of days between the filing
of this response and the requested effective date, implementation by November 11, 2026,
appears improbable. Accordingly, SPP modifies its requested effective date to December
1, 2026, to coincide with the commencement of the upcoming Winter Season. The revised
effective date provides additional time for Commission consideration of the proposed
revisions, while preserving SPP's ability to implement the interim energy adequacy
mechanism before the period in which it will be most needed. Accordingly, SPP
respectfully requests that the Commission accept the proposed Tariff revisions effective
December 1, 2026, rather than November 11, 2026, as originally requested.

V.     CONCLUSION

For all of the reasons discussed in this instant filing, the Commission should accept the
Tariff revisions submitted in this proceeding as just and reasonable.

 2.11.2         Reliability Unit Commitment and the Real-Time Balancing Market

                  For the RUC processes and RTBM, Market Participants must submit Resource
         Offers for all Resources to the extent these Resources are available. Market Participants
         must include in their Resource Offers the full amount of physical capacity available as
         reflected in the Resource’s submitted Maximum Normal Capacity Operating Limit and
         Maximum Emergency Capacity Operating Limit, or for MSRs, their Maximum
         Discharge Limit and Maximum Emergency Discharge Limit and/or their Minimum
         Charge Limit and Minimum Emergency Charge Limit.


2.11.2.1          Market Adequacy Evaluations for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
A.       On a post-Operating Day basis, and with respect to the SPP West Balancing Authority
         Area, the Transmission Provider will conduct two (2) market adequacy evaluations at the
         Asset Owner level for each Market Participant with Obligation, as described in Section
         2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE, in the SPP West Balancing Authority Area:
         (1)      When the Asset Owner’s Available Energy in any Operating Hour for the next
                  Operating Day, as identified by inputs into the Day-Ahead RUC, is less than the
                  Asset Owner’s Obligations for that same Operating Hour, the Transmission
                  Provider will assess a charge pursuant to Section 8.6.45 of this Attachment AE.
         (2)      When the Asset Owner’s Available Energy twenty (20) minutes prior to any
                  Operating Hour, as identified twenty (20) minutes prior to that Operating Hour, as
                  identified by the next Intra-Day RUC process described in Section 6.1 of this
                  Attachment AE, is less than the Asset Owner’s Obligations for that same
                  Operating Hour, the Transmission Provider will assess a charge pursuant to
                  Section 8.6.46 of this Attachment AE.
         (3)      For purposes of this Section, Available Energy consists of:
                  i.     Offers from Resources within the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
                         with commitment statuses described in Sections 4.1(10)(a), 4.1(10)(b), and
                         4.1(10)(c) of this Attachment AE. The Transmission Provider will
                         consider Offers as follows:
                         (a)     For an Offer from a Resource that is not an MSR or MCR, the
                                 Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limit;
              (b)    For an Offer from an MSR with a commitment status as described
                    in Sections 4.1(10)(a), 4.1(10)(b), or 4.1(10)(c) of this Attachment
                    AE, the Maximum Discharge Limit; and
             (c)    For an Offer from an MCR, the available configuration from that
                    MCR with the highest Maximum Economic Capacity Operating
                    Limit offered by the Market Participant.
      ii.    Offers from Resources within the SPP East Balancing Authority Area with
             one of the commitment statuses described in Sections 4.1(10)(a),
             4.1(10)(b), and 4.1(10)(c) of this Attachment AE where the Market
             Participant has notified the Transmission Provider of a transmission
             service right that contains a path across the West DC Tie. The
             Transmission Provider will consider Offers up to the MW quantity in the
             transmission service right as follows:
             (a)    For an Offer from a Resource that is not an MSR or MCR, the
                    Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limit;
             (b)    For an Offer from an MSR with a commitment status as described
                    in Sections 4.1(10)(a), 4.1(10)(b), or 4.1(10)(c) of this Attachment
                    AE, the Maximum Discharge Limit; and
             (c)    For an Offer from an MCR, the available configuration from that
                    MCR with the highest Maximum Economic Capacity Operating
                    Limit offered by the Market Participant.
      iii.   The greater of the Transmission Provider’s Variable Energy Resource
             MWh output forecast or the Real-Time Resource Billing Meter Quantity
             for the Market Participant’s Variable Energy Resources;
      iv.    Import Interchange Transaction Offers; and
      v.     Bilateral power purchases for the physical transfer of energy.
(4)   For purposes of this Section, an Asset Owner’s Obligations are within the SPP
      West Balancing Authority Area and will consist of:
      i.     Hourly average of Reported Load;
      ii.    Export Interchange Transaction Bids, excluding Real-Time Dispatchable
             Transactions;
       iii.   Regulation-Up and Contingency Reserve obligations estimates as
             described in Section 3.1.4(3) in this Attachment AE; and
      iv.    Bilateral power sales for the physical transfer of energy.
(5)   Market Participants for an Asset Owner with bilateral power purchases or power
      sales must provide notification to the Transmission Provider of the existence of
      the agreement supporting the transaction. The counterparty to the agreement must
      verify the existence of the agreement by 12:00 PM CT within four (4) calendar
      days following the Operating Day on which the transaction occurred. If day 4 falls
      on a Saturday or Sunday, the verification is due on the preceding Friday at noon.
      Upon receiving verification by the counterparty, the Transmission Provider will
      include the transacted MWs in the market adequacy evaluation for both purchaser
      and seller. If a party disputes the transaction to the Transmission Provider, then
      the transaction will not be used in the market adequacy evaluation for either the
      purchaser or seller. Upon request by the Transmission Provider, the Market
      Participant submitting the transaction must provide supporting documentation.
(6)   The Transmission Provider will consider a Self-Charging MSR, as described in
      Section 2.17.1 of this Attachment AE, as load and will include the hourly average
      of the Real-Time Load Billing Meter Quantity as described in Section 8.6.1 of
      this Attachment AE.
(7)   In the event an Operating Hour contains an RTBM system failure, as described in
      Section 8.3(5) of this Attachment AE, no market adequacy evaluation charges
      will be assessed.
(8)   In the event a market system failure occurs for the Day-Ahead RUC process
      described in Section 5.2 of this Attachment AE leading to the inability of SPP to
      calculate an Asset Owner’s Available Energy or Obligations in an Operating
      Hour, no market adequacy evaluation will occur as described in Section
      2.11.2.1(A)(1). In the event a market system failure occurs for the Intra-Day
      RUC process described in Section 6.1 of this Attachment AE leading to the
      inability of SPP to calculate an Asset Owner’s Available Energy or Obligations in
      an Operating Hour, no market adequacy evaluation will occur as described in
      Section 2.11.2.1(A)(2).
 B.   The provisions in this Section 2.11.2.1, as well as the associated charges and distributions
     described in Sections 8.6.45, 8.6.46, 8.6.47, and Section 8.6.48 of this Attachment AE,
     will cease to be effective on June 1st, 2027.
 3.3.1   Day-Ahead Market and RTBM SCED

        The SCED used in the Day-Ahead Market and RTBM produces both a dispatch solution
and a pricing solution. The dispatch solution and pricing solution are executed independent of
each other. The MW quantities used in settlements for the dispatch and clearing of Energy and
Operating Reserves result from the dispatch solution. Except where specified as DLMP, prices
used in settlements result from the pricing solution and will be specified as LMP, MCC, MCP,
MEC, and MLC. The DLMP results from the dispatch solution. The differences between the
dispatch solution and the pricing solution are:
 (1)    SCED dispatch solution

         (a)   Co-optimization of Energy and Operating Reserves is based on the Energy Offers
               and Bids and Operating Reserve Offers submitted by the Market Participants.

  (2)   SCED pricing solution

         (a)   For non-FSRs, co-optimization of Energy and Operating Reserves is based on the
               Energy Offers and Bids and Operating Reserve Offers submitted by the Market
               Participants.
         (b)   For FSRs committed by the Transmission Provider, including FSRs committed at
               the request of a local transmission operator, but not including self-committed
               FSRs, the Transmission Provider calculates a composite Energy Offer for use in
               the co-optimization of Energy and Operating Reserves. The composite Energy
               Offer will be calculated and applied as follows:

                 (i)   The Transmission Provider calculates a composite Energy Offer for an
                       FSR by modifying each price point on the Energy Offer Curve for each
                       market interval of the Minimum Run Time by adding amortized start-up
                       and no-load costs. For FSRs that are MSRs, the composite Energy Offer
                       applies only to the discharge portion of the Energy Offer curve.

                         1. The commitment costs (i.e. start-up cost and no-load cost) in effect
                               at the time of the commitment are amortized over the Maximum
                               Economic Capacity Operating Limit and the Minimum Run Time.
                         a. The start-up cost added to each breakpoint of the Energy
                            Offer Curve is calculated by dividing the Start-Up Offer by
                            the Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limit and by
                            the Minimum Run Time rounded up to the nearest interval.
                        b. The no-load cost added to each breakpoint of the Energy
                            Offer Curve is calculated by dividing the No-Load Offer by
                            the Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limit and by
                            the ratio of the number of intervals needed to meet the
                            Minimum Run Time to the number of intervals in an hour.
                2. The application of the composite begins with the commitment
                    interval and extends through the Minimum Run Time.
 (c)   In addition to dispatchable Bids and Offers, FSRs committed by the Transmission
       Provider, including FSRs committed at the request of a local transmission
       operator, but not including self-committed FSRs, will have their minimum
       operating limit relaxed to 0 MW.

 (d)   If the SPP Balancing Authority sheds load or requests emergency energy
       assistance imports, including imports requested for capacity support from a
       Reserve Sharing Group, due to a system-wide capacity issue, the net scheduled
       interchange and the load forecast used in the pricing solution will be offset
       according to Section 6.2.5 of this Attachment AE.

       For Day-Ahead Market and RTBM SCED, mitigation measures for Energy Offers
and Operating Reserve Offers, described under Sections 3.2 and 3.4 of Attachment AF of
this Tariff will be performed in the SCED pricing solution.
       An FSRs composite Energy Offer Curve will be subject to the Energy offer cap
described under Section 4.1.1 of this Attachment AE.
 8.6.45         Day-Ahead RUC Market Inadequacy Obligation Amount

         The Transmission Provider will calculate a Day-Ahead RUC amount for any Operating
Hour in which (1) an SPP West Balancing Authority Area Asset Owner’s Obligations, as
described in Section 2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE, are greater than the Asset Owner’s
Available Energy for that same Operating Hour; and (2) the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
for any portion of that Operating Hour is operating under Emergency Conditions. For the
purposes of this section, an SPP West Balancing Authority Area Asset Owner is an Asset Owner
with Obligations as described in Section 2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE. Such amount will be
calculated as follows:

         (1)   Market Inadequacy Obligation Operating Hour Amount = (Asset Owner’s Market
               Inadequacy MW) * (Minimum of (Either $1,000 or [Maximum of Either Average
               over the Operating Hour Real-Time Marginal Energy Component or Zero])

               (a)       An Asset Owner’s Market Inadequacy MW is equal to the Megawatt
                         amount by which an Asset Owner’s Obligations in the SPP West
                         Balancing Authority Area exceed its Available Energy as described in
                         Section 2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE.
 8.6.46          Pre-Operating Hour Market Inadequacy Obligation Amount

         The Transmission Provider will calculate an amount for any Operating Hour in which (1)
an SPP West Balancing Authority Area Asset Owner’s Obligations, as described in Section
2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE, are greater than the Asset Owner’s Available Energy for that
same Operating Hour; and (2) the SPP West Balancing Authority Area for any portion of that
Operating Hour is operating under Emergency Conditions. For the purposes of this section, an
SPP West Balancing Authority Area Asset Owner is an Asset Owner with Obligations as
described in Section 2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE. Such amount will be calculated as follows:

         (1)    Market Inadequacy Obligation Operating Hour Amount = (Asset Owner’s Market
                Inadequacy MW or Zero) * (Minimum of (Either $1,000 or Maximum of (Either
                Average over the Operating Hour Real-Time Marginal Energy Component or
                Zero)))

                (a)       An Asset Owner’s Market Inadequacy MW is equal to the Megawatt
                          amount by which a Market Participant’s Obligations in the SPP West
                          Balancing Authority Area exceed its Available Energy as described in
                          Section 2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE.
 8.6.47         Day-Ahead RUC Market Inadequacy Obligation Distribution

         (1)   The Transmission Provider will calculate a Day-Ahead RUC Market Inadequacy
               Obligation distribution amount for each Energy-adequate Asset Owner within the
               SPP West Balancing Authority Area for each Operating Hour to distribute the
               amount calculated under Section 8.6.45 of this Attachment AE. The calculation is
               as follows:

               (a)    Day-Ahead RUC Market Inadequacy Distribution Amount = ((Day-Ahead
                      RUC Market Inadequacy Obligation Amount) * (West BAA Asset Owner
                      Adequate Ratio Share)) * (-1).

                      (i)    The Day-Ahead RUC Market Inadequacy Obligation Amount shall
                             be equal to the sum of all payments made under Section 8.6.45 of
                             this Attachment AE for the Operating Hour.

                      (ii)   Asset Owner Adequate Ratio Share is defined as the ratio share of
                             each Energy-adequate Asset Owner’s share of adequate MWs
                             divided by all Energy-adequate Asset Owner’s adequate MW in
                             the SPP West Balancing Authority Area.

         (2)   For purposes of this section, an “Energy-adequate Asset Owner” is an Asset
               Owner whose Available Energy in any Operating Hour, as identified by inputs
               into the Day-Ahead RUC, is equal to or greater than the Asset Owner’s
               Obligations for that same Operating Hour as described in Section 2.11.2.1 of this
               Attachment AE.
 8.6.48         Pre-Operating Hour Market Inadequacy Obligation Distribution

         (1)   The Transmission Provider will calculate a Pre-Operating Hour Market
               Inadequacy Obligation distribution amount for each Energy-adequate Asset
               Owner within the SPP West Balancing Authority Area for each Operating Hour to
               distribute the amount calculated under Section 8.6.46 of this Attachment AE as
               follows:

               (a)    Pre-Operating Hour Market Inadequacy Distribution Amount = ((Pre-
                      Operating Hour Market Inadequacy Obligation Amount) * (West BAA
                      Asset Owner Adequate Ratio Share)) * (-1).

                      (i)    The Pre-Operating Hour Market Inadequacy Obligation Amount
                             shall be equal to the sum of all payments made under Section
                             8.6.46 of this Attachment AE for the Operating Hour.

                      (ii)   Asset Owner Adequate Ratio Share is defined as the ratio share of
                             each Energy-adequate Asset Owner’s share of adequate MWs
                             divided by all Energy-adequate Asset Owner’s adequate MW in
                             the SPP West Balancing Authority Area.

         (2)   For purposes of this section, an “Energy-adequate Asset Owner” is an Asset
               Owner whose Available Energy in any Operating Hour, as identified twenty (20)
               minutes prior to that Operating Hour, is equal to or greater than the Asset
               Owner’s Obligations for that same Operating Hour as described in Section
               2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE.

 2.11.2         Reliability Unit Commitment and the Real-Time Balancing Market

                  For the RUC processes and RTBM, Market Participants must submit Resource
         Offers for all Resources to the extent these Resources are available. Market Participants
         must include in their Resource Offers the full amount of physical capacity available as
         reflected in the Resource’s submitted Maximum Normal Capacity Operating Limit and
         Maximum Emergency Capacity Operating Limit, or for MSRs, their Maximum Discharge
         Limit and Maximum Emergency Discharge Limit and/or their Minimum Charge Limit and
         Minimum Emergency Charge Limit.


2.11.2.1          Market Adequacy Evaluations for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
A.       On a post-Operating Day basis, and with respect to the SPP West Balancing Authority
         Area, the Transmission Provider will conduct two (2) market adequacy evaluations at the
         Asset Owner level for each Market Participant with Obligation, as described in Section
         2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE, in the SPP West Balancing Authority Area:
         (1)      When the Asset Owner’s Available Energy in any Operating Hour for the next
                  Operating Day, as identified by inputs into the Day-Ahead RUC, is less than the
                  Asset Owner’s Obligations for that same Operating Hour, the Transmission
                  Provider will assess a charge pursuant to Section 8.6.45 of this Attachment AE.
         (2)      When the Asset Owner’s Available Energy twenty (20) minutes prior to any
                  Operating Hour, as identified twenty (20) minutes prior to that Operating Hour, as
                  identified by the next Intra-Day RUC process described in Section 6.1 of this
                  Attachment AE, is less than the Asset Owner’s Obligations for that same Operating
                  Hour, the Transmission Provider will assess a charge pursuant to Section 8.6.46 of
                  this Attachment AE.
         (3)      For purposes of this Section, Available Energy consists of:
                  i.     Offers from Resources within the SPP West Balancing Authority Area with
                         commitment statuses described in Sections 4.1(10)(a), 4.1(10)(b), and
                         4.1(10)(c) of this Attachment AE. The Transmission Provider will consider
                         Offers as follows:
                         (a)     For an Offer from a Resource that is not an MSR or MCR, the
                                 Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limit;
              (b)    For an Offer from an MSR with a commitment status as described
                    in Sections 4.1(10)(a), 4.1(10)(b), or 4.1(10)(c) of this Attachment
                    AE, the Maximum Discharge Limit; and
             (c)    For an Offer from an MCR, the available configuration from that
                    MCR with the highest Maximum Economic Capacity Operating
                    Limit offered by the Market Participant.
      ii.    Offers from Resources within the SPP East Balancing Authority Area with
             one of the commitment statuses described in Sections 4.1(10)(a), 4.1(10)(b),
             and 4.1(10)(c) of this Attachment AE where the Market Participant has
             notified the Transmission Provider of a transmission service right that
             contains a path across the West DC Tie. The Transmission Provider will
             consider Offers up to the MW quantity in the transmission service right as
             follows:
             (a)    For an Offer from a Resource that is not an MSR or MCR, the
                    Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limit;
             (b)    For an Offer from an MSR with a commitment status as described
                    in Sections 4.1(10)(a), 4.1(10)(b), or 4.1(10)(c) of this Attachment
                    AE, the Maximum Discharge Limit; and
             (c)    For an Offer from an MCR, the available configuration from that
                    MCR with the highest Maximum Economic Capacity Operating
                    Limit offered by the Market Participant.
      iii.   The greater of the Transmission Provider’s Variable Energy Resource
             MWh output forecast or the Real-Time Resource Billing Meter Quantity for
             the Market Participant’s Variable Energy Resources;
      iv.    Import Interchange Transaction Offers; and
      v.     Bilateral power purchases for the physical transfer of energy.
(4)   For purposes of this Section, an Asset Owner’s Obligations are within the SPP West
      Balancing Authority Area and will consist of:
      i.     Hourly average of Reported Load;
      ii.    Export Interchange Transaction Bids, excluding Real-Time Dispatchable
             Transactions;
       iii.   Regulation-Up and Contingency Reserve obligations estimates as described
             in Section 3.1.4(3) in this Attachment AE; and
      iv.    Bilateral power sales for the physical transfer of energy.
(5)   Market Participants for an Asset Owner with bilateral power purchases or power
      sales must provide notification to the Transmission Provider of the existence of the
      agreement supporting the transaction. The counterparty to the agreement must
      verify the existence of the agreement by 12:00 PM CT within four (4) calendar days
      following the Operating Day on which the transaction occurred. If day 4 falls on a
      Saturday or Sunday, the verification is due on the preceding Friday at noon. Upon
      receiving verification by the counterparty, the Transmission Provider will include
      the transacted MWs in the market adequacy evaluation for both purchaser and
      seller. If a party disputes the transaction to the Transmission Provider, then the
      transaction will not be used in the market adequacy evaluation for either the
      purchaser or seller. Upon request by the Transmission Provider, the Market
      Participant submitting the transaction must provide supporting documentation.
(6)   The Transmission Provider will consider a Self-Charging MSR, as described in
      Section 2.17.1 of this Attachment AE, as load and will include the hourly average
      of the Real-Time Load Billing Meter Quantity as described in Section 8.6.1 of this
      Attachment AE.
(7)   In the event an Operating Hour contains an RTBM system failure, as described in
      Section 8.3(5) of this Attachment AE, no market adequacy evaluation charges will
      be assessed.
(8)   In the event a market system failure occurs for the Day-Ahead RUC process
      described in Section 5.2 of this Attachment AE leading to the inability of SPP to
      calculate an Asset Owner’s Available Energy or Obligations in an Operating Hour,
      no market adequacy evaluation will occur as described in Section 2.11.2.1(A)(1).
      In the event a market system failure occurs for the Intra-Day RUC process
      described in Section 6.1 of this Attachment AE leading to the inability of SPP to
      calculate an Asset Owner’s Available Energy or Obligations in an Operating Hour,
      no market adequacy evaluation will occur as described in Section 2.11.2.1(A)(2).
 B.   The provisions in this Section 2.11.2.1, as well as the associated charges and distributions
     described in Sections 8.6.45, 8.6.46, 8.6.47, and Section 8.6.48 of this Attachment AE, will
     cease to be effective on June 1st, 2027.
 3.3.1   Day-Ahead Market and RTBM SCED

        The SCED used in the Day-Ahead Market and RTBM produces both a dispatch solution
and a pricing solution. The dispatch solution and pricing solution are executed independent of
each other. The MW quantities used in settlements for the dispatch and clearing of Energy and
Operating Reserves result from the dispatch solution. Except where specified as DLMP, prices
used in settlements result from the pricing solution and will be specified as LMP, MCC, MCP,
MEC, and MLC. The DLMP results from the dispatch solution. The differences between the
dispatch solution and the pricing solution are:
 (1)    SCED dispatch solution

         (a)   Co-optimization of Energy and Operating Reserves is based on the Energy Offers
               and Bids and Operating Reserve Offers submitted by the Market Participants.

  (2)   SCED pricing solution

         (a)   For non-FSRs, co-optimization of Energy and Operating Reserves is based on the
               Energy Offers and Bids and Operating Reserve Offers submitted by the Market
               Participants.
         (b)   For FSRs committed by the Transmission Provider, including FSRs committed at
               the request of a local transmission operator, but not including self-committed FSRs,
               the Transmission Provider calculates a composite Energy Offer for use in the co-
               optimization of Energy and Operating Reserves. The composite Energy Offer will
               be calculated and applied as follows:

                 (i)   The Transmission Provider calculates a composite Energy Offer for an FSR
                       by modifying each price point on the Energy Offer Curve for each market
                       interval of the Minimum Run Time by adding amortized start-up and no-
                       load costs. For FSRs that are MSRs, the composite Energy Offer applies
                       only to the discharge portion of the Energy Offer curve.

                         1. The commitment costs (i.e. start-up cost and no-load cost) in effect at
                               the time of the commitment are amortized over the Maximum
                               Economic Capacity Operating Limit and the Minimum Run Time.
                         a. The start-up cost added to each breakpoint of the Energy Offer
                            Curve is calculated by dividing the Start-Up Offer by the
                            Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limit and by the
                            Minimum Run Time rounded up to the nearest interval.
                        b. The no-load cost added to each breakpoint of the Energy Offer
                            Curve is calculated by dividing the No-Load Offer by the
                            Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limit and by the
                            ratio of the number of intervals needed to meet the Minimum
                            Run Time to the number of intervals in an hour.
                2. The application of the composite begins with the commitment interval
                    and extends through the Minimum Run Time.
 (c)   In addition to dispatchable Bids and Offers, FSRs committed by the Transmission
       Provider, including FSRs committed at the request of a local transmission operator,
       but not including self-committed FSRs, will have their minimum operating limit
       relaxed to 0 MW.

 (d)   If the SPP Balancing Authority sheds load or requests emergency energy assistance
       imports, including imports requested for capacity support from a Reserve Sharing
       Group, due to a system-wide capacity issue, the net scheduled interchange and the
       load forecast used in the pricing solution will be offset according to Section 6.2.5
       of this Attachment AE.

       For Day-Ahead Market and RTBM SCED, mitigation measures for Energy Offers
and Operating Reserve Offers, described under Sections 3.2 and 3.4 of Attachment AF of
this Tariff will be performed in the SCED pricing solution.
       An FSRs composite Energy Offer Curve will be subject to the Energy offer cap
described under Section 4.1.1 of this Attachment AE.
 8.6.45         Day-Ahead RUC Market Inadequacy Obligation Amount

         The Transmission Provider will calculate a Day-Ahead RUC amount for any Operating
Hour in which (1) an SPP West Balancing Authority Area Asset Owner’s Obligations, as described
in Section 2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE, are greater than the Asset Owner’s Available Energy
for that same Operating Hour; and (2) the SPP West Balancing Authority Area for any portion of
that Operating Hour is operating under Emergency Conditions. For the purposes of this section,
an SPP West Balancing Authority Area Asset Owner is an Asset Owner with Obligations as
described in Section 2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE. Such amount will be calculated as follows:

         (1)   Market Inadequacy Obligation Operating Hour Amount = (Asset Owner’s Market
               Inadequacy MW) * (Minimum of (Either $1,000 or [Maximum of Either Average
               over the Operating Hour Real-Time Marginal Energy Component or Zero])

               (a)    An Asset Owner’s Market Inadequacy MW is equal to the Megawatt
                      amount by which an Asset Owner’s Obligations in the SPP West Balancing
                      Authority Area exceed its Available Energy as described in Section 2.11.2.1
                      of this Attachment AE.
 8.6.46          Pre-Operating Hour Market Inadequacy Obligation Amount

         The Transmission Provider will calculate an amount for any Operating Hour in which (1)
an SPP West Balancing Authority Area Asset Owner’s Obligations, as described in Section
2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE, are greater than the Asset Owner’s Available Energy for that same
Operating Hour; and (2) the SPP West Balancing Authority Area for any portion of that Operating
Hour is operating under Emergency Conditions. For the purposes of this section, an SPP West
Balancing Authority Area Asset Owner is an Asset Owner with Obligations as described in Section
2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE. Such amount will be calculated as follows:

         (1)    Market Inadequacy Obligation Operating Hour Amount = (Asset Owner’s Market
                Inadequacy MW or Zero) * (Minimum of (Either $1,000 or Maximum of (Either
                Average over the Operating Hour Real-Time Marginal Energy Component or
                Zero)))

                (a)       An Asset Owner’s Market Inadequacy MW is equal to the Megawatt
                          amount by which a Market Participant’s Obligations in the SPP West
                          Balancing Authority Area exceed its Available Energy as described in
                          Section 2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE.
 8.6.47         Day-Ahead RUC Market Inadequacy Obligation Distribution

         (1)   The Transmission Provider will calculate a Day-Ahead RUC Market Inadequacy
               Obligation distribution amount for each Energy-adequate Asset Owner within the
               SPP West Balancing Authority Area for each Operating Hour to distribute the
               amount calculated under Section 8.6.45 of this Attachment AE. The calculation is
               as follows:

               (a)    Day-Ahead RUC Market Inadequacy Distribution Amount = ((Day-Ahead
                      RUC Market Inadequacy Obligation Amount) * (West BAA Asset Owner
                      Adequate Ratio Share)) * (-1).

                      (i)    The Day-Ahead RUC Market Inadequacy Obligation Amount shall
                             be equal to the sum of all payments made under Section 8.6.45 of
                             this Attachment AE for the Operating Hour.

                      (ii)   Asset Owner Adequate Ratio Share is defined as the ratio share of
                             each Energy-adequate Asset Owner’s share of adequate MWs
                             divided by all Energy-adequate Asset Owner’s adequate MW in the
                             SPP West Balancing Authority Area.

         (2)   For purposes of this section, an “Energy-adequate Asset Owner” is an Asset Owner
               whose Available Energy in any Operating Hour, as identified by inputs into the
               Day-Ahead RUC, is equal to or greater than the Asset Owner’s Obligations for that
               same Operating Hour as described in Section 2.11.2.1 of this Attachment AE.
 8.6.48         Pre-Operating Hour Market Inadequacy Obligation Distribution

         (1)   The Transmission Provider will calculate a Pre-Operating Hour Market Inadequacy
               Obligation distribution amount for each Energy-adequate Asset Owner within the
               SPP West Balancing Authority Area for each Operating Hour to distribute the
               amount calculated under Section 8.6.46 of this Attachment AE as follows:

               (a)    Pre-Operating Hour Market Inadequacy Distribution Amount = ((Pre-
                      Operating Hour Market Inadequacy Obligation Amount) * (West BAA
                      Asset Owner Adequate Ratio Share)) * (-1).

                      (i)    The Pre-Operating Hour Market Inadequacy Obligation Amount
                             shall be equal to the sum of all payments made under Section 8.6.46
                             of this Attachment AE for the Operating Hour.

                      (ii)   Asset Owner Adequate Ratio Share is defined as the ratio share of
                             each Energy-adequate Asset Owner’s share of adequate MWs
                             divided by all Energy-adequate Asset Owner’s adequate MW in the
                             SPP West Balancing Authority Area.

         (2)   For purposes of this section, an “Energy-adequate Asset Owner” is an Asset Owner
               whose Available Energy in any Operating Hour, as identified twenty (20) minutes
               prior to that Operating Hour, is equal to or greater than the Asset Owner’s
               Obligations for that same Operating Hour as described in Section 2.11.2.1 of this
               Attachment AE.
